about.metaDescription: Younghoon Kim, a frontend engineer who built an AI-assisted verification tool at EA and improved booking recovery and list performance at TicketLink, with 12 PRs merged into React Router, TanStack Query, and other open-source projects.
about.intro: I've worked as a frontend engineer at EA, NHN, and Pandora TV since July 2023. At EA, I built a tool that drafts verification checks with AI and lets operators review the evidence and make the final decisions. At TicketLink, I helped users check booking results after an interrupted session and improved list performance on older iPhones. I've contributed 12 merged PRs to React Router, TanStack Query, and other open-source projects.

items.developerExperience: Screens where operators review AI-generated verification checks alongside supporting evidence
items.reliableInterfaces: Recovering the result of an interrupted booking request and resuming failed work
items.runtimeBehavior: List performance on older iPhones and syncing server state when users return to a WebView
items.openSource: Open-source contributions that start with a reproduced bug and a test

ea.highlight1: Built operations tools on the FC Online SE team to help operators and QA prepare for verification. I agreed on processing rules with server developers and implemented the React screens and Node.js APIs.
ea.highlight2: Built an API that sends related documents, existing tests, and before-and-after values to an LLM to draft verification checks. Operators review the supporting passages, then accept, edit, or exclude suggestions and make the final decisions. Suggestions with insufficient evidence are flagged for review, and earlier edits are preserved after regeneration. After rollout, I used review records to address omissions and unnecessary suggestions.
ea.highlight3: Let QA choose an environment and target account state to run account creation, state setup, and final checks. The Node.js server records each step, while the React screen shows progress and failures. Before resuming failed work, the tool checks what the server has applied so it can continue from the required step without repeating completed work.

nhn.highlight1: Worked on the NHN Injeinc frontend team, improving how TicketLink users check booking results and how its lists perform.
nhn.highlight2: Temporarily saved the booking request ID and minimal recovery data in localStorage. When users returned in the same browser with a saved ID, the screen fetched that request’s status from the server and showed the result and next action. QA and I tested returns after payment authentication, browser restarts, and failed status requests before rollout.
nhn.highlight3: Reproduced a browser crash during long list scrolls on an older test iPhone. I introduced TanStack Virtual to keep only visible products and a small surrounding range in the DOM. The crash no longer reproduced on the same device with the same procedure, and an operator passed along confirmation from the original reporter.

pandora.highlight1: Sole frontend engineer for Cobak’s web and WebView screens, including post writing and editing, membership, and public pages.
pandora.highlight2: The app handled payment processing and completion notifications. On return, the WebView cancelled earlier requests with AbortController, invalidated related queries, and fetched payment and membership state from the server. It showed a pending screen during processing and fetched again on the app’s completion notification. I checked the pending, failed, and complete screens with component tests.
pandora.highlight3: Built manual save, a draft list, restore, and delete in the shared editor. I separated publishing from draft saving so users could reload posts saved on the server and continue writing. I manually checked first saves, updates, publishing restored drafts, new posts, and edits to existing posts, followed by operator QA.

openSource.heading: Merged open-source work
openSource.lead: I reproduced and fixed performance bottlenecks, runtime regressions, browser compatibility issues, and type problems in React Router, TanStack Query, and other React ecosystem projects. These are three examples from 12 merged PRs.

query.pr1Title: Reduced duplicate observer matching in useQueries
query.pr1Desc: In a separate measurement with 500 queries, findMatchingObservers calls fell from about 4,500 to about 2,000.

router.pr3Title: Fixed fetcher.submit treating plain objects as HTML elements
router.pr3Desc: Fixed plain objects with a tagName being mistaken for HTML elements and added a regression test.
router.pr5Desc: Made <Links /> pass crossOrigin through to fix CSS preload failures in CDN environments with CORS.

openSource.firsttx: FirstTx is a set of five npm packages for restoring screen state when users return to a CSR app and retrying individual steps. It also runs app-registered compensation functions for successful steps in reverse order. I maintain the docs, Playground, DevTools, and releases.
openSource.mentoring: Code review mentoring: four sessions in late 2025 for about 50 students across Programmers K-Digital Training cohorts.

stack.heading: Tools I use now
stack.line: I use React, TypeScript, and Next.js, with TanStack Query, React Router, and Zustand for state and routing. My build and test tools are Vite, Vitest, Playwright, and ESLint. For backend work, I use Node, Fastify, Prisma, and tRPC.
